title: When to Use ‘Some’ and Not ‘A’ or ‘An’ (1/3)
titleZh: 什麼時候該用 some 而不是 a 或 an (1/3)
summaryZh: 說明可數與不可數名詞的差別，以及單數名詞前該用 a 還是 an。
source: VOA Learning English (public domain) — Everyday Grammar

sentences.text: On this program, you have learned about count and non-count nouns.
sentences.zh: 在這個節目裡，你已經學過可數名詞和不可數名詞。

sentences.text: A count noun is something you can count and make plural, as in two trees, five girls, and so on.
sentences.zh: 可數名詞就是可以計數、可以變成複數的東西，例如兩棵樹、五個女孩等等。
不可數名詞在文法上算是單數。

sentences.text: For example, rice is non-count, but it is made up of many small pieces.
sentences.zh: 例如 rice（米）是不可數的，但它其實是由很多小顆粒組成的。

sentences.text: You can count glasses of water, but you would not normally count waters, unless you are talking about the many kinds of water on sale in some markets.
sentences.zh: 你可以數有幾杯水，但通常不會說 waters，除非你講的是市面上賣的那些不同種類的水。

sentences.text: We can count songs, but not music.
sentences.zh: 我們可以數歌曲，但不能數音樂。

sentences.text: So song is a count noun, while music is a non-count noun.
sentences.zh: 所以 song 是可數名詞，music 則是不可數名詞。

sentences.text: John wrote two songs last week.
sentences.zh: John 上禮拜寫了兩首歌。

sentences.text: His band plays new age music.
sentences.zh: 他的樂團演奏新世紀音樂。

sentences.text: With the singular form of count nouns, we use a before a word that begins with a consonant sound, and an before a word that begins with a vowel sound.
sentences.zh: 可數名詞用單數形式時，字首發子音的前面用 a，字首發母音的前面用 an。

sentences.text: There are exceptions, but this rule usually holds true.
sentences.zh: 雖然有例外，但這個規則大致上都成立。

sentences.text: They have an office on the first floor.
sentences.zh: 他們在一樓有一間辦公室。

sentences.text: I left a banana on the table for you.
sentences.zh: 我在桌上留了一根香蕉給你。

sentences.text: With the plural form of count nouns, we can use some instead of a or an.
sentences.zh: 可數名詞用複數形式時，我們可以用 some 來取代 a 或 an。
